tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Create (or connect) the user's free HelpySelf account from inside the conversation, so calls stop hitting the no-account limits (sign_in_required, too_many_files, daily_limit). Ask the user for their email first; never guess one. HelpySelf emails them a link; they press Allow; then call get_account_token. Free, no card. Pressing Allow accepts the Terms (https://helpyself.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://helpyself.com/privacy/); tell the user so. Results are provided as-is: check them before relying on them.

email.description: The user's own email address, as they gave it to you.

language.description: The user's language, for the page they confirm on. Defaults to en.

tools.name: get_account_token
tools.description: After create_account, once the user has pressed Allow in the email: returns the API token to send as Authorization: Bearer on later calls. Says 'waiting' until they have.

tools.name: buy_prepaid_runs
tools.description: Buy a pack of prepaid runs, cheaper than paying with a call (€0.50 for 3 runs). €5.00 buys 100 runs (€0.05 each), valid 365 days. A run is used only when a call would otherwise need a payment: an AI tool with no account or no credits left, or a call past a limit an account would lift. A call that fails gives its run back. Needs a payment-enabled client (Stripe Link agent wallet, MPP): call it, and the refusal carries the payment request in _meta under "org.paymentauth/payment-required"; ask the user to approve €5.00, then repeat the call with the credential. The key then pays automatically for the rest of this conversation. Only offer this when the user has hit a limit and wants to pay; a free account (create_account) is the free route.

tools.name: pdf_to_excel
tools.description: Every table in the PDF becomes a sheet, and every figure arrives as a number you can actually add up. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-to-excel (same tool, same answer, much faster). Results come from reading or converting a document and are not guaranteed: tell the user to check them, especially numbers, before relying on them. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The PDF to read, base64-encoded (a data: URL prefix is accepted). It needs a text layer: a scan with no text is refused with `no_text` rather than returning an empty workbook. Refused above 25 MB decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-to-excel (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

joinPages.description: Treat a table that carries on over a page break as one table, dropping the repeated heading row. On by default, because a statement split across twelve pages is one table; turn it off to get one sheet per page.

sheetName.description: What to call a tab the document did not name — `Table` gives Table 1, Table 2. A table the document headed keeps its own heading instead, trimmed to what Excel allows and made unique if it has to be.

includeText.description: Also keep everything that was not in a table — headings and paragraphs, in reading order, with the page each came from — as a sheet of its own. On by default: on an invoice the total being charged is a line of prose above the tables rather than a row inside one, so a workbook of only the grids has lost the number the document is about.

tools.name: pdf_to_word
tools.description: Convert a PDF to an editable Word document (.docx), with its tables and pictures. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-to-word (same tool, same answer, much faster). Results come from reading or converting a document and are not guaranteed: tell the user to check them, especially numbers, before relying on them. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The PDF to convert, base64-encoded (a data: URL prefix is accepted). It needs a text layer: a scan with no text is refused with `no_text` rather than turned into an empty document. Refused above 25 MB decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-to-word (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

keepPageBreaks.description: Start a new page in the Word document wherever the PDF started one. Off by default, so the text reflows and the Word page count may differ from the PDF's.

tools.name: epub_to_pdf
tools.description: Convert an EPUB e-book to PDF, with its chapters, bookmarks and links intact. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/epub-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The EPUB e-book (EPUB 2 or 3), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped if present. Copy-protected (DRM) books are refused with error 'drm', Kindle files with 'mobi'. Up to 50 MB once decoded. A very long book can exceed the memory an API call has; the in-browser tool on the website converts those. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/epub-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

pageSize.description: Paper size of the PDF. a5 is paperback-sized and reads like a book on screen; a4 or letter print on ordinary paper. Defaults to a5.

tools.name: excel_to_pdf
tools.description: Convert an Excel spreadsheet to PDF, with its dates, totals and column widths intact. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/excel-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The Excel workbook (.xlsx or .xlsm), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped if present. The old binary .xls format is refused with error 'xls'. Up to 25 MB once decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/excel-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

pageSize.description: document uses the paper size each sheet's page setup names (A4 when it names none). a4 or letter overrides it for every sheet. Orientation is chosen per sheet either way. Defaults to document.

gridlines.description: Draw the cell grid as Excel shows it on screen. A sheet whose author turned gridlines off stays without them. Defaults to true.

sheets.description: Names of the sheets (tabs) to include, in workbook order. Leave out to include every visible sheet; naming a hidden sheet includes it.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale for decimal and thousands separators and month names, e.g. de-DE shows 1.234,50. Excel draws these from the reader's computer, not the file. Defaults to en-US.

tools.name: powerpoint_to_pdf

Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/powerpoint-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The PowerPoint presentation (.pptx, .ppsx, .potx or .pptm), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped if present. The old binary .ppt format is refused with error 'ppt'. Up to 50 MB once decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/powerpoint-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

includeHidden.description: Include slides marked hidden in PowerPoint, in their place. Defaults to false, which leaves them out as a slide show does and lists 'hidden' in skipped.

tools.name: word_to_pdf
tools.description: Convert a Word document (.docx or .doc) to PDF, keeping its layout, tables and pictures. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/word-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The Word document, base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped if present. A .docx is expected, and the older binary .doc is recognised from its bytes too. Up to 25 MB once decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/word-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

pageSize.description: document keeps the paper size and margins the file was written for. a4 or letter overrides them with that paper and fixed margins, which re-wraps every paragraph. Defaults to document.

tools.name: excel_to_csv
tools.description: Convert an Excel workbook to CSV: every sheet, quoted properly, with dates as Excel shows them. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/excel-to-csv (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The Excel workbook (.xlsx or .xlsm), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped if present. The old binary .xls format is refused with error 'xls'. Up to 50 MB once decoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/excel-to-csv (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

delimiter.description: The field separator. semicolon is what Excel uses in locales whose decimal point is a comma (German, French, Danish…). Defaults to comma.

values.description: shown writes each cell as Excel displays it (dates, currency, percentages, separators of `locale`); plain writes the stored value: numbers with a full stop and no thousands separators, dates as ISO 8601. Defaults to shown.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale for decimal and thousands separators and month names when values is shown, e.g. de-DE gives 1.234,50. Defaults to en-US.

sheets.description: Names of the sheets (tabs) to convert, in workbook order. Leave out to convert every visible sheet; naming a hidden sheet includes it.

skipHidden.description: Leave out rows and columns that are hidden in Excel. Defaults to false, which keeps them, as Excel's own Save as CSV does.

tools.name: address_labels
tools.description: Turn a CSV, an Excel sheet or a list of addresses into a print-exact PDF for label sheets (Avery 5160, L7160, Zweckform 3475 and more). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The addresses. Either a CSV/TSV table with a header row (one address per row; the separator is detected), or plain addresses one after another with a blank line between them (each line of a block is one line on the label). Leave out when sending `xlsx`.

xlsx.description: An Excel workbook (.xlsx), base64-encoded, instead of `text`. The first visible sheet is read unless `sheet` names another; its first row is the header. Up to 10 MB once decoded.

sheet.description: Which worksheet of `xlsx` to read, by its tab name.

format.description: How to read `text`: table (CSV/TSV with a header row), blocks (addresses separated by blank lines), or auto (the default), which picks table when every line has the same number of separators.

header.description: A table's first row holds the column names. Defaults to true; with false, columns are named {1}, {2}…

lines.description: What each line of a label says, with column names in braces, e.g. ["{First name} {Last name}", "{Street}", "{City}, {State} {ZIP}"]. Column names match the header in any case; {1}, {2}… are column numbers. A line whose columns are all empty is left out. Omit to have it guessed from the header (name, company, street, town line, country; e-mail and phone columns are left out). Ignored for blocks.

template.description: The label sheet, by the code on its pack. Known: 5160, 5161, 5162, 5163, 5164, 5167, 5168, 5126, L7160, L7161, L7159, L7162, L7163, L7173, L7165, L7651, 3475, 3474, 3422, 3481, 3424, 3425, 3484, 3427, 4360, and codes with the same layout (8160, 5960, J8160, 3490, HERMA 4453…). Brand words are ignored ("Avery 5160" works). Use "custom" with `custom` for any other sheet. Defaults to 5160 (US Letter, 30 a sheet).

left.description: From the sheet's left edge to the first label's left edge.

top.description: From the sheet's top edge to the first label's top edge.

pitchX.description: Horizontal pitch: one label's left edge to the next one's (label width plus the gap), in `custom.unit`.

pitchY.description: Vertical pitch: one label's top edge to the next one's (label height plus the gap), in `custom.unit`.

skip.description: Label positions already used on the first sheet, counted across then down from the top-left. Defaults to 0.

copies.description: Labels per address, side by side — e.g. 30 fills a 5160 sheet with one return address. Defaults to 1.

offsetX.description: Moves everything right (positive) or left, in mm, for a printer that prints off-centre. Defaults to 0.

offsetY.description: Moves everything down (positive) or up, in mm. Defaults to 0.

fontSize.description: Text size in points, or auto (the default): the largest up to 12 pt that fits every label, never below 6 pt.

align.description: Text alignment within each label. Defaults to left.

boldFirstLine.description: Print each label's first line (usually the name) in bold. Defaults to false.

outlines.description: Draw a thin grey outline of every label, for a test print on plain paper held against a real sheet. Defaults to false.

addressStyle.description: Only used when `lines` is guessed: us writes "City, ST ZIP", eu writes "Postcode City", br writes "Cidade - UF" then "CEP …". Defaults to us.

examples.text:

tools.name: currency_converter
tools.description: An exchange rate calculator using the European Central Bank's official daily rate. An estimate for planning, not financial, tax or legal advice; say so when giving the figures. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

amount.description: How much of fromCurrency to convert, in major units (dollars, not cents). Negative is allowed, since a refund is a conversion too. A plain numeric string such as "10" is read as the number.

fromCurrency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the currency the amount is in, such as USD. Case does not matter. Only currencies the European Central Bank quotes daily are known; an unknown code returns an error naming it.

toCurrency.description: The ISO 4217 code to convert into, such as EUR. The rate used is the ECB cross rate for the day, and the whole day's rate table comes back with the answer.

tools.name: email_reminder
tools.description: Schedule an email to the user's own inbox (and optionally a signed webhook) at a date and time, once or repeating daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly or yearly. For reminders that must happen after the chat ends. Free with a free HelpySelf account. With no account, offer to make one: call it anyway and the refusal explains how to create it right in this chat (create_account). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

action.description: create (default) schedules a reminder. list returns the caller's reminders with their tokens. cancel removes one by token, so it will not be sent.

token.description: The reminder's token, from create or list. Required for cancel.

subject.description: What to be reminded of, used as the email subject: 'Renew the car insurance'. Up to 120 characters, one line. Required for create.

message.description: Optional longer text for the email body, up to 2000 characters. Plain text.

at.description: When to send, ISO 8601. With an offset or Z ('2026-12-04T09:00:00+01:00') it is an exact instant. Without one ('2026-12-04T09:00') it is a wall-clock time in timeZone — use that form for what a person said ('Friday at nine'). A date alone means 09:00 that day. At least one minute ahead. Give either at or inMinutes for create.

inMinutes.description: Alternative to at: send this many minutes from now, e.g. 90.

timeZone.description: The person's IANA time zone, e.g. 'Europe/Copenhagen' or 'America/New_York'. Used to read an `at` without an offset and to keep a repeat at the same local time across daylight saving. Default UTC.

repeat.description: none (default) sends once. daily, weekdays (Mon–Fri), weekly (same weekday), monthly (same day of the month, or its last day in a shorter month) and yearly repeat at the same local time until cancelled.

email.description: Send the email to the account's own address (default true). Set false for a webhook-only reminder.

webhookUrl.description: Pro: also POST to this public https:// URL when it is due. The JSON body is {event, token, subject, message, dueAt, occurrence}; the header X-HelpySelf-Signature is sha256=<hex HMAC of the raw body with the webhookSecret returned by create>.

locale.description: Language of the email's own wording: en, de, es, fi, fr, it, nl, pl or pt. Default en.

tools.name: pregnancy_calculator
tools.description: A due date calculator that also tells you how many weeks you are today. General information only, not medical advice; say so, and suggest a health professional for decisions. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

lmpDate.description: First day of the last menstrual period as YYYY-MM-DD. Everything is counted from this date by Naegele's rule (280 days to the due date), shifted by `cycleLength`. Refused if it is in the future or more than 48 weeks ago.

asOfDate.description: The date to measure weeks, days and trimester to, as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit and the server uses today's date in UTC, which can be a day out near midnight; send the reader's own local date when you have it.

cycleLength.description: Average menstrual cycle length in days. 28 is what Naegele's rule assumes; each day longer moves the due date and the estimated conception date one day later.

tools.name: private_chat
tools.description: Makes a private chat link (WebRTC, browser to browser, end-to-end encrypted) for your person to open and send on. No messages pass through the API. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

locale.description: The language the chat page is shown in: en, de, es, fi, fr, it, nl, pl or pt. Default en. Use the language of the person you are giving the link to.

tools.name: private_video_call
tools.description: Makes a private video call link for two (WebRTC, browser to browser, encrypted, no account or app) for your person to open and send on. No audio or video passes through the API. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

locale.description: The language the video call page is shown in: en, de, es, fi, fr, it, nl, pl or pt. Default en. Use the language of the person you are giving the link to.

tools.name: screen_share_online
tools.description: Makes a screen share link for two (WebRTC, browser to browser, encrypted, no account or app): your person shares a screen, window or tab and one viewer watches on any device. No video passes through the API. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

locale.description: The language the screen share page is shown in: en, de, es, fi, fr, it, nl, pl or pt. Default en. Use the language of the person you are giving the link to.

tools.name: photo_gallery
tools.description: Free photo hosting: one shared gallery page with its own link and QR code, layout and optional password. It can be made with no photos: the result includes addPhotosUrl, a page where the owner adds them from any browser. Free with a free HelpySelf account. With no account, offer to make one: call it anyway and the refusal explains how to create it right in this chat (create_account). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

action.description: create (default) makes a new gallery and returns its link and addPhotosUrl; with no fileIds it starts empty and the user adds the photos in their browser at addPhotosUrl. list returns the caller's live galleries with their tokens. edit changes one by token — only the fields you send change; send fileIds to replace the picture list in a new order. delete stops sharing one by token, and with deleteFiles also deletes its pictures.

token.description: The gallery's token, from list or from create's answer. Required for edit and delete.

deleteFiles.description: delete only: also delete the gallery's pictures from storage. A picture another live gallery still shows is kept. Omit to stop sharing and keep the files.

removePassword.description: edit only: remove the gallery's password so the link opens without one.

title.description: The heading shown at the top of the gallery page, up to 120 characters. Required for create.

intro.description: The subtitle, shown as plain text under the heading; never rendered as a link. Omit for none.

fileIds.description: Optional for create: omit it when you cannot send the photos (in a chat you can see them but not send them), and the user adds them in the browser at addPhotosUrl. For edit, the whole new picture list in order (omit to keep it). Ids of files the signed-in caller already owns, in the order they should appear. Can you run shell commands? Upload each photo first to https://helpyself.com/api/v1/files with curl -F "file=@<path>" -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token from get_account_token>', and use the id it returns; the gallery stores no bytes of its own. Up to 200 pictures; duplicates are shown once. The link never outlives the files it shows.

items.description: The id of a file in the caller's own storage, as returned on upload.

captions.description: Captions matched to `fileIds` by position, so the third caption belongs to the third file. Use null or an empty string to leave one uncaptioned. Omit for none.

items.description: The caption for the file at the same position, or null for none.

columns.description: Pictures per row on a wide screen (default 3), treated as a maximum: a phone shows at most two across and a tablet three, whatever is set here.

rowsPerPage.description: Split the gallery into pages of this many rows (rows x columns pictures each), with Previous/Next buttons. Omit to show every picture on one page.

layout.description: grid (default) crops every tile to a square for a uniform wall; masonry keeps each picture's own proportions and packs them.

duration.description: How long the public link works, from now: 1h, 24h, 7d or 30d (default for create), and on Pro also 90d, 1y or never. For edit, omit to keep the current end. Always cut short if any of the files expires sooner.

password.description: A password visitors must enter before any picture is fetched. Omit, or send an empty string, for an open link.

tools.name: sitemap_generator
tools.description: Crawl a public website politely (robots.txt, noindex, canonical, nofollow) and get its sitemap.xml with lastmod, plus broken links, redirects and noindex pages. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

url.description: The site to crawl, e.g. 'https://example.com/' or 'example.com'. Links are followed on that host only. Public addresses only. Required to start a crawl; leave it out when sending a cursor.

cursor.description: Continue a crawl: the cursor returned by the previous call while done was false. Send it alone; the address and options are remembered for an hour.

respectNoindex.description: Leave pages marked noindex (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag) out of the sitemap. Default true.

respectCanonical.description: Leave a page out when its canonical tag names another page on the site, and crawl that one instead. Default true.

respectNofollow.description: Do not follow rel="nofollow" links, nor any link on a page whose meta robots says nofollow. Default true.

tools.name: website_monitor
tools.description: Check whether a website is up right now from outside (status, response time, redirects), or watch it and email the account owner when it goes down and when it is back. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

action.description: check (default) loads the address once now and reports status, response time and redirects; no account needed. watch keeps checking it on a schedule and emails the account owner when it goes down and when it is back (needs a signed-in account). list returns the account's watched sites with their state and recent outages. remove stops watching one by token.

url.description: The page to check, e.g. 'https://example.com/' or 'example.com'. Public addresses only. Required for check and watch.

expectText.description: Optional text the page must contain (case-insensitive), so an error page that still answers 200 OK counts as down. E.g. 'Add to basket'.

token.description: The monitor's token, from watch or list. Required for remove.

locale.description: Language of the down/up emails: en, de, es, fi, fr, it, nl, pl or pt. Default en.

tools.name: video_channel
tools.description: Upload your videos once, then share your whole channel or just one video with a link. No ads, no algorithm. Free with a free HelpySelf account. With no account, offer to make one: call it anyway and the refusal explains how to create it right in this chat (create_account). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

action.description: add (default) puts an uploaded video on one of the caller's channels and returns its link and the channel's link. list returns every channel with its videos and tokens. edit changes one video by token (title, description, listed, or channelToken to move it). remove deletes one video and its file. createChannel makes a new channel (name, about). renameChannel changes a channel's name or about text. deleteChannel deletes a channel with every video on it.

channelToken.description: Which channel, from list or createChannel. add: the channel to put the video on (omit to use the newest channel, or make a first one if there is none). edit: the channel to move the video to. renameChannel and deleteChannel: required.

fileId.description: add only: the id of a video file the caller already owns. Upload it first with POST /v1/files/upload-url, a PUT of the bytes, then POST /v1/files/confirm. An H.264 MP4 plays in every browser; other formats may not play on every device.

posterFileId.description: add only: optional id of an uploaded image (JPEG or PNG) shown before the video plays.

token.description: edit and remove: the video's token, from list or from add's answer.

title.description: The video's title, up to 100 characters. Required for add.

description.description: Text shown under the video, up to 2000 characters. Plain text.

listed.description: true (default) shows the video on its channel page. false makes it link only (unlisted): reachable by its own link and not shown on the channel.

durationMs.description: add only: the length in milliseconds, if known.

width.description: add only: the width in pixels, if known.

height.description: add only: the height in pixels, if known.

name.description: createChannel and renameChannel: the channel's name, up to 60 characters. add: used only if the caller has no channel yet and one is made.

about.description: createChannel and renameChannel: a line shown under the channel's name, up to 500 characters.

locale.description: add and createChannel: the language a new channel's pages are written in (en, de, es, fr, it, nl, pl, pt, fi). Default en.

tools.name: secret_santa
tools.description: Type in the names, keep couples apart, and give everyone a private link that shows only who they drew. Free with a free HelpySelf account. With no account, offer to make one: call it anyway and the refusal explains how to create it right in this chat (create_account). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

title.description: The group's name, shown at the top of everybody's page: 'Family Christmas 2026'. Up to 80 characters.

items.description: One person's name, as the others know them.

people.description: Everybody taking part, 3 or more. Names are compared case-insensitively, so the same name twice is refused — add an initial to tell two Annas apart. How many one draw may hold depends on the caller's plan; a group over it is refused with the number.

exclusions.description: Pairs who must not draw each other, such as couples. Works both ways. Every name must be one of `people`. Refused if the rules leave no possible draw.

items.description: Two people who must not draw each other, e.g. ['Anna', 'Bo'].

budget.description: The spending limit as people should read it, e.g. '€25' or 'around 200 kr'. Optional.

exchangeDate.description: The day presents are exchanged, as YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

note.description: A line shown to everybody, e.g. where and when you meet. Optional.

reach.description: edges (the default) removes only background connected to the image border, so enclosed areas like the hole in a letter or a window behind someone stay. everywhere removes every pixel within tolerance wherever it is.

to.description: Unit id to convert to, from the same category and the same list of ids as from.

xml.description: The XML document to work on.

mode.description: format re-indents it, one node per line; minify puts it on one line; validate only reports whether the tags nest and close, with the line of the first fault. None of them checks against a schema. Defaults to format.

indent.description: Spaces per nesting level when formatting, or "tab" for one tab per level. Ignored by minify and validate. Defaults to 2.

keepComments.description: Keep <!-- --> comments when formatting; false drops them. Defaults to true.

data.description: The PDF to render, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. name.description: Base name for the image files; a .pdf ending is dropped and pages are named <name>-01.png and so on, zero-padded to the page count. Also names the ZIP when `archive` is on.

type.description: Image format for every page. PNG is lossless; JPEG and WebP are much smaller and honour `quality`.

size.description: Longest edge of each image in pixels: thumbnail 480, screen 1280, print 2480. A request estimated at more than 120 megapixels in total is refused before rendering, so ask for fewer pages or a smaller size.

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP, 0.1 to 1, where 1 is the largest file and the best picture. Ignored for PNG.

pages.description: Which pages to render, counted from 1: single pages and ranges separated by commas, such as "1-3, 7, 12-", where an open end runs to the last page. Omit for every page.

archive.description: Return one ZIP of every image, base64-encoded in `data`, instead of an `images` array with one base64 string per page. Easier to handle for a long document.

data.description: The PDF to rebuild, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. name.description: Base name for the output file; a .pdf ending is dropped and the response names it <name>.pdf.

order.description: Source page numbers, 1-based, in the order they should appear, as "3, 1, 2". A range may run backwards, so "10-1" reverses a ten-page document. Leave a page out to delete it and repeat one to duplicate it. Omit to keep every page in its current order.

rotations.description: Extra clockwise rotation per source page, as {"2": 90}. Added to whatever rotation the page already has, and keyed by source page rather than output position, so it holds good after a reorder.

propertyNames.description: A source page number, 1-based, as a string key.

additionalProperties.description: Clockwise degrees to add to that page.

tools.name: pdf_split

data.description: The PDF to split, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 20 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. name.description: Base name for the output files; a .pdf ending is dropped. extract mode names the result <name>-extracted.pdf, single mode <name>-page-N.pdf per page.

mode.description: extract returns one PDF holding the selected pages; single returns one PDF per selected page. `files` in the response is an array either way.

pages.description: Which pages to take, counted from 1: single pages and ranges separated by commas, such as "1-3, 7, 12-", where an open end runs to the last page. The order given is kept, so "3, 1" puts page 3 first. Omit for every page.

tools.name: avif_converter
tools.description: AVIF to JPG, and JPG to AVIF — the format that halves a photograph. Can you run shell commands? A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The image file's bytes, base64-encoded: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or AVIF. At most 30 MB decoded. An animated GIF is converted to a still of its first frame, and the response says so with note: "animation-dropped". Send the whole file as it is, up to 32 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/avif-converter (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

name.description: The original filename. Only used to name the result: its extension is swapped for the output format's, so photo.jpg comes back as photo.avif.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data. The image pipeline reads all of these; the actual format is taken from the bytes, so a wrong value here is not fatal.

format.description: The format to produce. AVIF is what the tool is for; WebP, JPEG and PNG exist so an AVIF can be converted back to something older software opens.

quality.description: Encoder quality, 1 (smallest, roughest) to 100 (largest). Ignored for PNG, which is lossless. The default of 60 is deliberate: AVIF at 100 is often larger than the JPEG it replaces.

maxWidth.description: Scale the image down so its width is at most this many pixels, keeping the aspect ratio. Never enlarges. Omit to keep the original dimensions.

tools.name: images_to_pdf
tools.description: JPG to PDF and PNG to PDF — photos to PDF, in the order you choose. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/images-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The image's filename. Its extension is a fallback for telling JPEG from PNG.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes: image/jpeg or image/png. Only these two can be embedded.

data.description: The image file as base64. A data: URL prefix is tolerated and stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 21 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/images-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

items.description: One image, which becomes one page.

images.description: The images in page order, one page each, at most 100 of them.

pageSize.description: The paper size. 'fit' makes each page exactly the image's own pixel size, with no margins or letterboxing; 'a4' and 'letter' put every image on that fixed page, scaled to fit and centred.

orientation.description: Page orientation for 'a4' and 'letter': 'portrait' or 'landscape' for every page, or 'auto' to turn a page landscape when its image is wider than tall. Ignored for 'fit'.

margin.description: White space around the image on 'a4' and 'letter' pages, in PDF points (72 per inch; 144 is two inches). Ignored for 'fit'.

tools.name: pdf_rotate
tools.description: Rotate PDF pages the right way up — sideways or upside-down. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-rotate (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The PDF to rotate, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 20 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. name.description: Base name for the output file; a .pdf ending is dropped and the response names it <name>-rotated.pdf.

angle.description: Clockwise rotation in degrees, added to whatever rotation each page already has. Lossless: nothing is re-rendered. A quarter turn when omitted.

pages.description: Which pages to rotate, counted from 1: single pages and ranges separated by commas, such as "1-3, 7, 12-", where an open end runs to the last page. Omit for every page.

only.description: Filter the selected pages by their current orientation: landscape turns only pages wider than tall, portrait only pages taller than wide, all turns every selected page. The response lists which pages actually turned.

tools.name: base64
tools.description: Base64 encode and decode text instantly, with full Unicode support. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The text to encode, or the Base64 to decode, depending on action. Encoding goes through UTF-8 first, so accents, emoji and CJK survive. Decoding accepts standard or URL-safe Base64, with or without padding, and ignores whitespace.

action.description: encode turns text into Base64; decode turns Base64 back into UTF-8 text. Defaults to encode.

urlSafe.description: When encoding, use the URL-safe alphabet (RFC 4648 section 5): + and / become - and _, and the = padding is dropped, as in JWTs. Ignored when decoding, which detects either alphabet.

tools.name: cookie_checker
tools.description: A cookie checker that shows what a website sets, and whether Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite are on. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

url.description: The public website to check, for example https://example.com. A bare hostname is read as https. The page is fetched as a normal browser would and every Set-Cookie header it returns is parsed and judged. Private, loopback and non-http addresses are refused.

tools.name: image_cropper
tools.description: Crop image online — drag the box, or type an exact size in pixels. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-cropper (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. The result keeps its stem with the output format's extension.

type.description: The MIME type of the source image: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. x.description: The crop box's left edge, in pixels from the left of the source image.

y.description: The crop box's top edge, in pixels from the top of the source image.

width.description: The crop box's width in source pixels. A box that runs past the image is clamped to fit inside it, and never below 8 pixels.

height.description: The crop box's height in source pixels, clamped to the image like width.

format.description: The output format. 'auto' keeps PNG and WebP sources in their own format, so transparency survives, and writes everything else as JPEG.

quality.description: Encoder quality from 0.1 to 1 for JPEG and WebP output; lower is smaller and softer. PNG is lossless and ignores it.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send this or fileId, not both. Anything a vision model can read works: a photo of a page, a screenshot, a scan. Send the whole file as it is: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-to-text (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

fileId.description: The id of an image already uploaded to the caller's account, to read instead of data. Needs a signed-in caller; the upload is consumed by the run. Most scripts should send data instead.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp or image/gif. Ignored when fileId is used, since the stored type wins.

mode.description: What to return: 'text' is the words in reading order and nothing else; 'markdown' keeps headings and lists, which suits a document scan; 'table' transcribes a table as CSV.

language.description: The language the text is most likely in, e.g. 'Danish', as a hint to the model. It is not a constraint: what is actually in the picture is transcribed.

tools.name: readability_score
tools.description: Readability score for any text — Flesch–Kincaid, Gunning fog index and more. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: English prose to score, at least 20 words. Scored with Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning fog, SMOG, ARI and Coleman-Liau, which are averages over sentence and syllable counts, so a short passage gives a rough answer.

examples.text: The library opens at nine on weekdays. Children can borrow up to ten books at a time, and adults may keep a book for three weeks before they need to bring it back or renew it online.

tools.name: barcode_generator
tools.description: A barcode generator for EAN-13, UPC-A, EAN-8 and Code 128 — check digit included. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: What to encode. For ean13, upca and ean8 this is digits only: 12, 11 or 7 of them and the check digit is worked out, or one more and it is verified (a wrong one is refused rather than drawn). For code128 it is any printable ASCII up to 80 characters.

symbology.description: Which barcode standard to draw. ean13 (13 digits, the retail default worldwide), upca (12 digits, North American retail), ean8 (8 digits, small packaging), code128 (letters, digits and punctuation, for labels and logistics).

scale.description: Width of the narrowest bar in pixels; every other width and the quiet zones are multiples of it, so this sets the overall size. 3 is about right for a screen.

height.description: Height of the bars in pixels. The printed number and the longer guard bars add to the total height of the SVG when showText is true.

showText.description: Print the encoded value underneath the bars, as a retail barcode always does. False gives bars only.

tools.description: A barcode scanner online — read a barcode or QR code from a photo or screenshot. Can you run shell commands? A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The image file's bytes, base64-encoded: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP. SVG is refused here (the server cannot rasterise it); convert it to PNG first. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/barcode-reader (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes, such as image/png. Optional and only used to reject something that is plainly not an image; the format is otherwise read from the bytes.

tools.name: collage_maker

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. HEIC and AVIF are read on the tool's page only.

data.description: The photo's file bytes, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is tolerated and stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 10 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/collage-maker (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

focusX.description: Which part of the photo stays in view when it is cropped to fill its space, left to right: 0 keeps the left edge, 0.5 the centre, 1 the right edge.

focusY.description: The same from top to bottom: 0 keeps the top, 0.5 the centre, 1 the bottom.

images.description: The photos in order, at most 20. The first fills the first space (the big one in the big-* layouts), and so on.

layout.description: grid: an even grid that adapts to however many photos there are. two-side: 2 side by side. two-stack: 2 stacked. big-left-2: one big photo on the left with 2 beside it. big-top-2: one big on top with 2 below. big-left-3: one big on the left with 3 beside it. big-top-3: one big on top with 3 below. A fixed layout uses as many photos as it has spaces; extra photos are left out and missing ones leave a space in the background colour.

shape.description: The finished picture's shape: square (1:1), portrait (4:5, an Instagram post), landscape (16:9) or story (9:16, for stories and reels).

size.description: The long edge of the finished picture in pixels: 1080 or 2048. The tool's page also makes 4096.

spacing.description: The border between and around the photos: none, thin, medium or wide. It scales with the picture's size.

corners.description: Corner rounding on each photo: square, soft or round.

background.description: The colour behind and between the photos, as #rrggbb.

format.description: jpeg (smaller, best for photos) or png (lossless).

tools.name: contrast_fixer
tools.description: A colour contrast fixer — the nearest accessible colour that passes WCAG AA. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

foreground.description: The text colour, as hex, rgb(), hsl() or a CSS colour name.

background.description: The colour behind the text, in the same forms as foreground.

level.description: The WCAG grade to reach. AA is normal body text at 4.5:1, AA_LARGE is large text at 3:1, AAA is 7:1 and AAA_LARGE is 4.5:1. Defaults to AA.

adjust.description: Which colour may change. Only its lightness moves; hue and saturation are kept. 'either' tries both and returns the smallest change first. Defaults to either.

tools.name: csv_to_json
tools.description: CSV to JSON and back — turn a spreadsheet export into clean, readable JSON. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The data to convert: CSV text when direction is csv-to-json, or a JSON array of objects or arrays when it is json-to-csv. Quoted fields, embedded newlines and doubled quotes are handled.

direction.description: Which way to convert. Defaults to csv-to-json. Going to CSV, the columns are the union of every object's keys and rows are joined with CRLF.

delimiter.description: The field separator: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe. 'auto' (the default) picks whichever appears most on the first line outside quotes when reading CSV, and writes a comma when producing it. The one used is returned.

header.description: Treat the first CSV row as column names, or write one when producing CSV. On by default. Off, every row is data and shape falls back to arrays.

shape.description: The JSON produced from CSV: 'objects' keyed by column name (duplicate names get a _2 suffix), or 'arrays' of values in column order. Defaults to objects.

trim.description: Strip whitespace from both ends of every field and column name when reading CSV. On by default.

typed.description: Convert fields that look like numbers, true/false or null to those JSON types, and empty fields to null. Off by default so postcodes and codes like 007 stay strings.

indent.description: Spaces of indentation in the JSON output. 0 puts it all on one line. Defaults to 2. Ignored when producing CSV.

tools.name: csv_viewer
tools.description: A CSV viewer that reads CSV or TSV text into rows and columns, detects the separator, and can filter and sort. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

csv.description: The CSV or TSV text to read. Quoted fields, embedded line breaks and doubled quotes are handled. Returns the separator, row and column counts, a summary of each column (number or text, empty cells, min and max) and the first rows, optionally filtered and sorted.

delimiter.description: The field separator: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe. 'auto' (the default) picks whichever appears most on the first line outside quotes. The one used is returned.

header.description: Treat the first row as column names. On by default.

filter.description: Keep only rows where some cell contains this text, ignoring case. Empty (the default) keeps every row. rowCount stays the whole file; matching counts the kept rows.

sortBy.description: Sort by this column: its header name (any case) or its 1-based number. Numbers like 1,234.50, 12 % or $3 sort as numbers when the whole column reads that way; empty cells go last. Omit to keep the file's order.

descending.description: Sort largest or last first. Ignored without sortBy.

rows.description: How many rows to return after filtering and sorting, 0 to 100. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: font_converter
tools.description: Convert TTF and OTF to WOFF2 or WOFF for the web, and WOFF2 back to TTF. Subset it, get the @font-face CSS. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/font-converter (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The font file's bytes, base64-encoded: TrueType (.ttf), OpenType (.otf), WOFF or WOFF2. At most 2 MB decoded; larger fonts (CJK families) convert on the web page. The kind is read from the bytes, not the name. Font collections (.ttc/.otc) are refused. Send the whole file as it is, up to 2 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/font-converter (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

name.description: The original filename. Only used to name the result and the url() in the CSS: Inter-Regular.ttf converted to WOFF2 comes back as Inter-Regular.woff2.

format.description: What to produce. woff2 is what a website should serve (smallest, every current browser); woff is the older web format for very old browsers; ttf or otf gives back the plain desktop font from a WOFF/WOFF2. The outlines are never converted, so ttf and otf both return the font's own kind: .otf for CFF outlines, .ttf for TrueType.

subset.description: Which characters to keep. none keeps the whole font. latin and latin-ext are Google Fonts' ranges (latin-ext adds Central European letters such as ą, ł, ő, ș). text keeps only the characters in `text`; ranges keeps the Unicode ranges in `ranges`. Layout features, kerning, hinting and variable axes are kept for what remains.

text.description: With subset: "text", the characters to keep, as plain text (for example a logo's wording or a page's headings). Each distinct character is kept once.

ranges.description: With subset: "ranges", Unicode ranges to keep, CSS-style: "U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+20AC". Wildcards like U+4?? are accepted.

tools.name: image_resizer
tools.description: A photo resizer for any size — JPEG, PNG, WebP or an iPhone HEIC. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-resizer (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. The result is named after its stem with the new size appended, e.g. 'photo-800x600.jpg'.

type.description: The MIME type of the source image: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-resizer (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

mode.description: How the new size is given: 'dimensions' uses width and height in pixels, 'percentage' scales both sides by percentage and ignores width and height.

width.description: The target width in pixels, for the 'dimensions' mode. With keepAspect on, giving a width sets the height from it and any height given is ignored. Omitted with keepAspect off, the source width is kept.

height.description: The target height in pixels, for the 'dimensions' mode. With keepAspect on it only applies when width is omitted, and then sets the width from it.

percentage.description: The scale for the 'percentage' mode, as a percentage of the source size per side: 50 halves both edges, 100 leaves it as is. Over 100 needs allowUpscale.

keepAspect.description: Keep the source proportions in 'dimensions' mode, so one of width or height drives the other. Set false to stretch to an exact width and height.

format.description: The output format: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. Omit it to keep the source format.

quality.description: Encoder quality from 0.1 to 1 for JPEG and WebP output; lower is smaller and softer. PNG is lossless and ignores it.

allowUpscale.description: Allow a result larger than the source on either side, up to 10000 pixels. Off by default, so enlarging is refused with an explanation rather than adding blur.

tools.name: invoice_generator
tools.description: A free invoice generator that makes a real PDF — no watermark, no sign-up. An estimate for planning, not financial, tax or legal advice; say so when giving the figures. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

from.description: The sender's name and address as free text; line breaks are kept.

to.description: The customer's name and address as free text; line breaks are kept.

description.description: What the line is for, as printed on the invoice: 'Consulting, March', 'Logo design'.

quantity.description: How many units of the line. Fractions are allowed: 1.5 hours, 0.25 days.

unitPriceCents.description: The price per unit in the currency's minor unit, so 1999 means 19.99. Integers only. A negative value makes a discount line.

items.description: One line on the invoice; its amount is quantity times unitPriceCents.
The lines to bill, in the order they should appear.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. 'USD', 'EUR', 'DKK'. It decides the symbol and decimals shown; an unknown code is refused with an error rather than guessed.

issueDate.description: The date the invoice is issued, as YYYY-MM-DD. The due date is counted from it, and its year goes into the generated invoice number.

paymentTermsDays.description: How many days after issueDate payment is due. 0 means due on the issue date.

sequence.description: The position in your invoice series, used to build the number as INV-<year>-<sequence padded to 4 digits>, e.g. 7 in 2026 gives INV-2026-0007. Ignored when number is given.

number.description: Your own invoice number, printed as given. Overrides the one built from sequence.

taxPercent.description: Tax added on top of the subtotal, as a percentage: 25 adds a quarter. 0 leaves the total equal to the subtotal.

taxLabel.description: What the tax line is called on the invoice: 'VAT', 'MwSt', 'Moms', 'GST'.

notes.description: Free text printed under the totals: payment details, bank account, terms, a thank-you. Empty prints nothing.

locale.description: The BCP 47 locale the amounts are formatted in, e.g. 'en-US' writes 1,234.56 and 'da-DK' writes 1.234,56. It does not translate the labels.

pdf.description: Include the rendered PDF as base64 in pdfBase64. Set false to get only the number, due date and totals, which is faster and much smaller.

tools.name: signature_maker
tools.description: A signature maker: draw or type yours, saved with a transparent background. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

x.description: Horizontal position, increasing to the right, in pad units.

y.description: Vertical position, increasing downwards as in SVG, in pad units.

items.description: One sampled pen position.
One pen stroke: its points in drawing order. A single point draws a dot.

strokes.description: The drawing as a list of strokes, each a list of points in the order the pen visited them, in any consistent unit. At most 20000 points in total. The result is an SVG path, so the units only matter relative to strokeWidth.

strokeWidth.description: Line thickness, in the same units as the points. It also sets the scale of padding and of the simplify tolerance.

colour.description: Ink colour as a hex value, #rgb or #rrggbb. Anything else falls back to #111111 rather than being written into the SVG.

smooth.description: Draw quadratic curves through the points instead of straight segments between them, which stops a signature looking ruler-drawn.

trim.description: Fit the SVG viewBox tightly to the ink. False keeps the pad's origin, so empty space above and left of the signature is kept and it sits off-centre when placed.

padding.description: Space left around the ink when trimming, measured in stroke widths rather than points units, so 2 at a strokeWidth of 3 is 6 units on every side.

simplify.description: Drop points that lie almost on the line between their neighbours (tolerance of a quarter of strokeWidth). Shrinks the path a great deal and steadies the smoothing.

tools.name: stall_booking
tools.description: One link, on your own site or sent — vendors pick their own stall. Free with a free HelpySelf account. With no account, offer to make one: call it anyway and the refusal explains how to create it right in this chat (create_account). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

title.description: The market's name, shown as the heading of the public booking page vendors book on. A successful call publishes that page under the caller's account and returns its URL, so call once per market.

note.description: A line shown under the title on the booking page: doors open, where to park, what not to bring.

date.description: The day the market is held, as YYYY-MM-DD with no time or zone. It must not be in the past, and the booking page is deleted daysAfter days after it.

venueId.description: The id of a hall the caller has already drawn in the venue editor. Given, the market uses that hall's shape and hand-placed stalls, and hallWidth, hallDepth, stalls and the stall sizes are ignored. Omitted, a plain rectangle is laid out from hallWidth, hallDepth and stalls, which are then all required.

hallWidth.description: Width of the hall in centimetres, so 2000 is twenty metres. Required when no venueId is given; a value under two metres is refused as a typo.

hallDepth.description: Depth of the hall in centimetres. Required when no venueId is given.

stalls.description: How many stalls to lay out in the rectangle. Required when no venueId is given. If fewer fit at the given stall size, fewer are made rather than the stalls being shrunk, and the response says how many. A free account is limited to a smaller market than Pro.

stallWidth.description: Width of one stall in centimetres, along the row. 180 is a standard trestle table.

stallDepth.description: Depth of one stall in centimetres, front to back.

gap.description: The aisle between stalls in centimetres, both between neighbours in a row and between rows. 120 fits prams and wheelchairs.

backToBack.description: Lay rows out in pairs with their backs together and the aisle only between pairs, so the public cannot walk behind a seller. Fits more stalls in the same hall than a plain grid.

backGap.description: Space between the two backs of a paired row in centimetres, for the sellers' chairs and stock. Only used when backToBack is true; it is not the aisle.

price.description: What one stall costs, in the currency's minor unit (cents, pence, øre), so 25000 is 250.00. Never a decimal amount. 0 means the stalls are free.

currency.description: What the price is in. An ISO code such as "DKK" or "EUR" is formatted properly; any other text ("kr", "beer tokens") is printed as given beside the number.

units.description: How the hall is shown to people, in metres or in feet. Display only: every dimension in this call is centimetres either way.

paymentDetails.description: How a vendor is to pay, in the organiser's own words, shown to them after they book: a bank account, a MobilePay number, "cash on the day". No card processing is involved.

holdHours.description: How many hours a booked stall is held while the vendor pays, at most a week. If the organiser has not marked it paid by then, the stall is released for someone else to book.

daysAfter.description: How many days after the market date the booking page stays up. After that it is deleted, along with the vendors' names and contact details.

tools.name: url_encoder
tools.description: A URL encoder and decoder for links and query strings, percent-encoded properly. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The text to encode, the percent-encoded string to decode, or the URL to parse, depending on action.

action.description: encode percent-encodes text; decode reverses it; parse splits a complete URL (scheme included) into protocol, host, path, query parameters and hash, and ignores mode.

mode.description: component encodes or decodes every reserved character, as encodeURIComponent does, which is right for one query value. full leaves the characters that structure a URL (/ ? & = : #) alone, as encodeURI does, which is right for a whole address. Ignored by parse.

tools.name: bulk_image_resizer
tools.description: A bulk image resizer: resize many images at once. Can you run shell commands? A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The original filename. Echoed back unchanged as the result's name.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data: JPEG, PNG or WebP. Also the output type when format is keep.

data.description: The image file's bytes, base64-encoded. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. maxEdge.description: The longest side of the result in pixels. The image is scaled down to fit inside this on its longer edge, keeping its aspect ratio. Never enlarges: an image already within the bound is returned as it is, with unchanged: true.

format.description: The output format. keep (the default) re-encodes in the same type as the input; the others convert. JPEG has no transparency, so transparent areas are flattened onto white.

quality.description: Encoder quality for JPEG and WebP, 0.1 (smallest) to 1 (largest). Has no effect on PNG, which is lossless.

tools.name: contrast_grid
tools.description: A contrast grid for your whole palette — every pairing checked against WCAG. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

palette.description: The colours to check against each other, as hex, rgb(), hsl() or CSS colour names, separated by newlines, commas or spaces. CSS custom-property names are ignored, duplicates are dropped, and 2 to 24 distinct colours are needed.

level.description: The WCAG grade a pairing must clear to count as passing: AA is 4.5:1, AA_LARGE is 3:1, AAA is 7:1, AAA_LARGE is 4.5:1. Every cell still reports its own ratio and grade; this only decides the pass count. Defaults to AA.

tools.name: image_converter
tools.description: Convert between JPEG, PNG and WebP, one file or many, with transparency flattened onto a colour you choose. HEIC and AVIF are browser-only and not accepted here. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-converter (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. The result keeps its stem with the target format's extension.

type.description: The MIME type of the source image: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. HEIC, AVIF, TIFF and BMP are not accepted over the API.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. target.description: The format to convert to: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. It must differ from type; converting to the same format is refused. AVIF is not available over the API.

quality.description: Encoder quality from 0.1 to 1 when the target is JPEG or WebP; lower is smaller and softer. PNG is lossless and ignores it.

background.description: A CSS colour painted behind transparent areas when converting to JPEG, which has no transparency. Defaults to white. Ignored for PNG and WebP targets.

tools.name: markdown_to_html
tools.description: Turn Markdown into clean HTML, with a preview you can trust. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The Markdown to convert: CommonMark plus the GitHub extensions (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks). Links are limited to http, https, mailto, tel, ftp and relative URLs; other schemes are dropped.

allowHtml.description: Pass any raw HTML in the Markdown through to the output instead of escaping it. Off by default, which is the safe choice: inline HTML can carry a script, so only turn this on for Markdown you wrote yourself.

headingIds.description: Give every heading an id derived from its text, made unique within the document, so a table of contents can link to it. Off, and headings carry no id.

breaks.description:
Turn every single newline into a
, the way chat apps do. Off, and only a line ending in two spaces breaks; other newlines join into the same paragraph.

tools.name: wheel_of_names
tools.description: A spinning wheel of names — paste a list, spin, and get one fair winner. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

names.description: The entries to draw from, one per line. Blank lines and surrounding spaces are ignored; a name listed twice has two chances.

draws.description: How many winners to draw. Without removeWinner each draw is from the full list, so the same name can win more than once. Defaults to 1.

removeWinner.description: Take each winner out of the list before the next draw, so no name wins twice. Drawing stops early if the list runs out; remaining in the response lists who is left.

tools.name: word_counter
tools.description: A word counter and character counter, updating as you type. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The text to count. Returns characters with and without spaces, words, sentences, paragraphs (split on blank lines), lines, reading and speaking time in minutes, and the most frequent words with common ones left out.

tools.name: yaml_to_json
tools.description: Convert a config file to JSON, or JSON back to readable YAML. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The document to convert: YAML when direction is yaml-to-json, JSON when it is json-to-yaml. A YAML file holding several --- documents becomes a JSON array.

direction.description: yaml-to-json parses YAML and returns JSON; json-to-yaml parses JSON and returns YAML. Defaults to yaml-to-json.

indent.description: Spaces of indentation in the output. For JSON, 0 gives a single line; YAML output always indents by at least 1. Defaults to 2.

sortKeys.description: Sort object keys alphabetically at every level, so two configs can be compared. Off by default, which keeps the input's order.

tools.name: ascii_table
tools.description: The full ASCII table, with the control codes explained rather than left blank. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

search.description: What to look up: a single character ("A"), a decimal code ("65"), hex ("0x41", "U+0041", "\x41"), binary ("0b01000001"), octal ("0o101"), an HTML entity ("&"), an abbreviation ("LF") or part of a name ("line feed", "sep"). Numbers return one entry; names return every match, best first. Plain digits are always decimal. Empty (the default) returns the whole table.

includeExtended.description: Also include codes 128 to 255, read as ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1). ASCII proper stops at 127, so a search for a higher code finds nothing unless this is true.

tools.name: binary_translator
tools.description: A binary translator both ways — binary to text, text to binary, hex and decimal too. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

input.description: Plain text, or bytes written as binary, hex, decimal or octal. Groups may be separated by spaces or commas; hex also accepts 0x prefixes and unspaced pairs. Every other representation of the same bytes comes back at once, so there is no direction to choose. Text is treated as UTF-8, so "é" is two bytes.

readAs.description: How to read input. auto (the default) works it out: only 0s and 1s in whole bytes is binary, hex digits with a letter or 0x is hex, several zero-padded pairs is hex, several numbers up to 255 is decimal, anything else is text. Octal is never guessed, since "17" is valid octal and decimal, so name it explicitly. Byte values over 255 are refused.

targetKb.description: The size the output must not exceed, in kilobytes of 1,024 bytes, as upload limits mean it. The highest quality that fits is found by re-encoding; if none does, the response says so and suggests a scale factor to shrink the pixels by instead.

tools.name: cron_expression
tools.description: Read a cron expression in plain English, and see exactly when it will next run. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

expression.description: A five-field crontab expression (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) such as '*/15 9-17 * * MON-FRI', or a shorthand like @daily or @hourly. timezone.description: The IANA time zone the schedule is read in, such as Europe/Copenhagen. Cron means wall-clock time, so the run times change with it. Defaults to UTC, and an unrecognised name falls back to UTC.

count.description: How many upcoming runs to list, strictly after now, each as a wall-clock ISO string without an offset plus a readable form. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: gradient_generator
tools.description: A CSS gradient generator for linear, radial and conic — copy the code straight out. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

colour.description: Any CSS colour: a hex code, rgb(), hsl() or a named colour.

position.description: Where along the gradient this colour sits, as a percentage from 0 to 100. Omit it and CSS spaces the stop evenly between its neighbours.

items.description: One colour stop.

stops.description: The colours in order, from 2 to 16 of them.

shape.description: For radial gradients only: 'circle' keeps the rings round, 'ellipse' stretches them to the box. Ignored for linear and conic.

repeating.description: Emit the repeating-* variant, which tiles the gradient over the box instead of stretching it once. Only visible when the stops have explicit positions short of 100.

items.description: One digest algorithm.

tools.name: html_to_markdown

tools.name: http_status_codes

tools.name: morse_code_translator

type.description: The MIME type of the source image: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif (first frame), image/bmp or image/tiff. SVG, AVIF and HEIC are not accepted here.
