sizes.description: Pixel sizes to pack into the one .ico file, from 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256. Defaults to 16, 32, 48 and 256, which covers browser tabs, the Windows taskbar and Explorer.

fit.description: How a non-square image becomes a square icon: pad keeps the whole picture and fills the sides with transparency; crop fills the square from the centre and cuts the long side. Square images are unaffected.

tools.name: receipt_scanner
tools.description: Receipt scanner: photograph a receipt or invoice and get the shop, date, items, VAT and total as data. Free with a free HelpySelf account (5 AI credits a month, 1 per run). With no account, call it anyway: the refusal explains how to make the free account right in this chat (create_account), or a client with an agent wallet can pay €0.50 with the call for 3 runs, or €0.05 a run with buy_prepaid_runs. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/receipt-scanner (same tool, same answer, much faster). Results come from reading or converting a document and are not guaranteed: tell the user to check them, especially numbers, before relying on them. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: A photo, scan or screenshot of one receipt or invoice, base64-encoded, in the format given by type. Send this or fileId, not both. For a PDF invoice, turn the page into an image first (pdf-to-images). Send the whole file as it is, up to 20 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/receipt-scanner (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

fileId.description: The id of an image already uploaded to the caller's account, to read instead of data. Needs a signed-in caller; the upload is consumed by the run. Most callers should send data.

type.description: The MIME type of the bytes in data: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp or image/gif.

language.description: The language the receipt is most likely in, e.g. 'Danish', as a hint. Not a constraint.

tools.name: duplicate_line_remover
tools.description: Remove duplicate lines, blanks and stray spaces from a list in one pass. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The lines to de-duplicate, separated by any line ending. The result is the text with repeats removed, in the original order unless sort says otherwise, plus counts of what was dropped.

caseSensitive.description: Treat Apple and apple as different lines. Off by default, so they count as the same line and only the kept one survives.

trimLines.description: Strip whitespace from both ends of every line before comparing and before output. On by default. Off, trailing spaces make two lines different.

removeBlank.description: Drop empty lines entirely rather than keeping one of them. On by default.

keep.description: Which occurrence of a repeated line survives: 'first' keeps it where it first appeared, 'last' keeps it at its final position. Defaults to first.

sort.description: Order of the output: 'none' keeps the input order, 'asc' and 'desc' sort alphabetically with locale-aware, numeric-aware comparison (item2 before item10), 'length' sorts shortest line first. Defaults to none.

onlyDuplicates.description: Invert the tool: return only the lines that appeared more than once, one entry each in order of first appearance, and leave the unique lines out. Off by default.

tools.name: screen_recorder
tools.description: Plans a screen recording: the bitrate, file size and longest safe length for a given picture size and frame rate. The recording itself is made on the web page. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

width.description: Width of the area being recorded, in pixels. Bitrate scales with the pixel count, so a shared window costs far less than a full 4K screen.

height.description: Height of the area being recorded, in pixels.

frameRate.description: Frames per second to capture at. Bitrate scales with it, and 30 is enough for screen content, which changes little between frames.

quality.description: How much data to spend, as bits per pixel per frame: "high" is 0.10 and keeps text crisp at 1080p, "balanced" is 0.05 with readable text and slight banding, "small" is 0.02 for a long recording that has to be emailed. There is a floor of 400 kbit/s whatever the picture size.

withAudio.description: Whether the recording carries an audio track. True adds a fixed 128 kbit/s of Opus to the size estimate and shortens the safe duration accordingly.

seconds.description: The planned length of the recording, in seconds, used only to estimate the file size and to say whether it is past the point where a browser tab runs out of memory (about 512 MB held in the tab). The bitrate and safe duration do not depend on it.

tools.name: sleep_calculator
tools.description: A sleep calculator that works backwards from when you have to be up. General information only, not medical advice; say so, and suggest a health professional for decisions. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

time.description: A 24-hour clock reading with a colon, such as "07:30" or "23:15". No date or time zone is involved. "7.30" or "7:30 pm" is refused.

timeIs.description: What time is: "wake" means it is the alarm and bedtimes are returned, most sleep first; "bedtime" means it is when you go to bed and wake times are returned, earliest first. 4 options come back, for 3 to 6 cycles.

cycleMinutes.description: Length of one sleep cycle in minutes. 90 is the adult average; real cycles run roughly 70 to 120 and differ between people.

fallAsleepMinutes.description: Minutes spent falling asleep after going to bed, subtracted from a bedtime or added to a wake time. Defaults to 15.

tools.name: sqlite_viewer
tools.description: Open a SQLite database (.sqlite, .db) read-only: list its tables and views with row counts and columns, read rows sorted and filtered, run one SELECT, or get a table as CSV. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/sqlite-viewer (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The SQLite database file (.sqlite, .sqlite3, .db), base64-encoded; a data: URL prefix is stripped. Up to 20 MB once decoded. It is opened read-only and nothing in it is changed. Send the whole file as it is, up to 20 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/sqlite-viewer (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

table.description: A table or view to read rows from, by name. Leave out (and leave out query) to get the first table's rows.

query.description: One read-only SQL statement to run instead of reading a table: SELECT, WITH, VALUES, EXPLAIN or a PRAGMA that only reads. INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, ATTACH and the like are refused. SQLite syntax.

filter.description: With table: keep only rows where some column contains this text, ignoring case. Empty keeps every row.

sortBy.description: With table: the column to sort by. NULLs go last.

descending.description: With sortBy: largest or last first.

offset.description: With table: rows to skip first, for paging. Defaults to 0.

rows.description: How many rows to return, 0 to 500. Defaults to 20. Ignored when output is csv.

output.description: rows (the default) returns the rows as JSON arrays beside the column names. csv returns the whole table or query result as CSV text instead, up to five million characters.

tools.name: subnet_calculator
tools.description: A subnet calculator that gets /31 and /32 right, which most do not. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

network.description: An IPv4 address with a prefix length ("192.168.1.10/24"), an address and a dotted mask separated by a space ("10.0.0.1 255.0.0.0"), or a bare address, which is read as /24. Octets with leading zeros are refused, as is a mask that is not a run of ones followed by zeros.

tools.name: svg_minifier
tools.description: An SVG minifier that strips editor clutter and scripts, without touching the artwork. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The SVG source as text. Anything without an <svg> element is refused.

precision.description: Decimal places kept on coordinates and other numeric attributes; -1 leaves numbers untouched. Two is enough for an icon and is where most of the saving comes from.

removeMetadata.description: Strip <metadata>, Inkscape and Sodipodi elements, attributes and namespace declarations: editor bookkeeping that draws nothing.

removeTitleDesc.description: Strip <title> and <desc>. Off by default because they are the accessible name and description a screen reader reads out.

removeScripts.description: Strip <script> elements, on* event handlers, javascript: links and the <a> elements around them, so the output is safe to serve as a file. On by default.

removeUnusedIds.description: Drop id attributes nothing inside the file refers to. Off by default because CSS or JavaScript in the embedding page may target them, which cannot be checked here.

removeXmlDeclaration.description: Strip the <?xml ?> declaration, any DOCTYPE and the editor's Generator comment.

collapseWhitespace.description: Remove whitespace between tags and collapse runs of it inside them. The content of text, style, title and desc elements is left as it is.

shortenColours.description: Shorten six-digit hex colours that can be written in three: #ffffff becomes #fff.

examples.text: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><!-- icon --><circle cx="12.000" cy="12.000" r="10" fill="#ffffff"/></svg>

tools.name: timezone_converter
tools.description: A time zone converter and world clock — one time, every city at once. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

date.description: The calendar date on the wall clock in fromZone, as YYYY-MM-DD.

time.description: The wall-clock time in fromZone, 24-hour, as HH:MM. A time the clocks skip is moved forward and flagged; one that happens twice is read as the first.

fromZone.description: IANA zone name the date and time are read in, e.g. "America/New_York". Abbreviations such as EST or CST are not accepted, since they are ambiguous.

items.description: An IANA zone name such as "Asia/Tokyo".

toZones.description: IANA zone names to read the same moment in. Each comes back with its own date, time, abbreviation, UTC offset and whether it is a day ahead or behind.

tools.name: typing_test
tools.description: A typing speed test that shows both your raw and your real WPM. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

target.description: The passage the person was supposed to type. Compared against typed character by character, position by position.

typed.description: What was actually typed, exactly as entered. Shorter than target is fine; the untyped rest counts as pending.

elapsedMs.description: Time taken, in milliseconds. Words per minute counts five characters as a word; 0 scores 0 wpm rather than dividing by zero.

includeCharacters.description: Also return a verdict for every character of target: correct, incorrect or pending. Off by default because it is thousands of strings for a minute of typing.

tools.name: webcam_test
tools.description: A webcam test that tells you what the other end will actually see. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

width.description: Frame width in pixels. With height it decides the resolution grade, judged on the shorter side so portrait counts, and the aspect ratio.

frameRate.description: Frames per second, if already known. Omit it and pass frameTimestampsMs to have it measured; omit both and smoothness comes back null.

frameTimestampsMs.description: Arrival times of consecutive frames, in milliseconds. Needs at least two; the rate is derived from first to last rather than from any single gap. Ignored when frameRate is given.

items.description: When one frame arrived, in milliseconds.

pixels.description: One frame as RGBA bytes, four values per pixel, 0-255, as a canvas getImageData returns them; the length must be a multiple of four. Used to measure brightness and the blown-out fraction. Send a downsample of up to 100,000 pixels, such as 64x64: it gives the same verdict as a full frame.

items.description: One channel value, 0-255.

brightness.description: Average brightness of the frame, 0 (black) to 1 (white), if measured yourself. Ignored when pixels is given.

blownFraction.description: Fraction of the frame burnt out to white, 0 to 1, if measured yourself. Ignored when pixels is given. This is what tells a backlit subject from a well-lit one.

tools.name: case_converter
tools.description: A text case converter: camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case and more. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The text to convert. It may already be in any case: camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, acronyms like HTTPServer and digits are all split into words before being rebuilt.

target.description: The case to produce: camel (helloWorld), pascal (HelloWorld), snake (hello_world), constant (HELLO_WORLD), kebab (hello-world), title (Hello World, small words like "of" kept lower unless first or last), sentence (first letter of each sentence capitalised, punctuation kept), upper or lower (the whole text, punctuation kept). Omit to get every case at once as a list.

tools.name: regex_tester
tools.description: A regex tester for regular expressions, run safely against your own text. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

pattern.description: A JavaScript regular expression, bare, without surrounding slashes; flags go in flags. At most 500 characters, which is shorter than the page allows.

flags.description: The standard JavaScript flags as one string, such as "gi". The default "g" returns every match; without it only the first match is returned.

text.description: The text to run the pattern against, at most 20000 characters. Matches are returned with their index and capture groups, and stop after 1000.

tools.name: remove_line_breaks
tools.description: Remove line breaks from text that was hard-wrapped, and keep the paragraphs. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The hard-wrapped text to reflow — copied out of a P D F, an email or a terminal.

mode.description: What to keep. "paragraphs" removes the breaks inside a paragraph and keeps the blank line between paragraphs, which is almost always what is wanted; "all" collapses everything to a single line.

joinWith.description: What replaces a removed break. "nothing" is for scripts written without spaces between words, where a space would be wrong.

keepLists.description: Leave a line that starts a list item on its own line. A hard-wrapped document is full of them, and joining a bulleted list into a sentence loses the only structure it had.

mendHyphens.description: Rejoin a word the line break split: "inter-" then "national" becomes "international". Only applied where the next line starts lower-case, so a real hyphen in "well-Known" is left alone.

tools.name: timestamp_converter
tools.description: A Unix timestamp converter — timestamps to dates, and dates back to timestamps. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

value.description: A Unix timestamp or a date. A bare number is read as seconds, or as milliseconds once it reaches 100000000000 (1e11); negative means before 1970. Anything else is parsed as a date string such as 2026-08-03T12:00:00Z.

timeZone.description: IANA zone name, e.g. "Europe/Copenhagen", used for the local reading and the day of the week. Defaults to UTC, and an unknown name falls back to UTC rather than failing.

tools.name: aspect_ratio_calculator
tools.description: Find the aspect ratio of any size, or the width or height that keeps a ratio. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

width.description: Width in any unit (usually pixels). With height and no ratio: returns the aspect ratio of that size. With a ratio and no height: returns the height that keeps the ratio.

height.description: Height in the same unit as width. With width and no ratio: returns the aspect ratio. With a ratio and no width: returns the width that keeps the ratio.

ratio.description: An aspect ratio to resize to, written "16:9", "4:3", "2.39:1" or "16/9". Give it with exactly one of width or height and the other side comes back as exact, rounded (whole) and even (for video encoders).

nearestWithinPercent.description: When describing a size: how far, in percent, it may be from a common named ratio (16:9, 4:3, 21:9 …) and still be reported as `nearest`. 1366 × 768 is 0.05 % from 16:9. Past this, nearest is null.

tools.name: braille_translator
tools.description: A braille translator both ways — text to Grade 1 braille, and braille back to text. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: Print text to transcribe into Grade 1 braille, or braille (the Unicode braille block, U+2800 to U+28FF) to turn back into print.

direction.description: Which way to translate. "auto" reads braille back into print and transcribes anything else; "toBraille" and "toText" force one direction.

tools.name: color_converter
tools.description: A colour converter: HEX to RGB, RGB to HEX, and either to HSL. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

color.description: The colour to convert, in any CSS form: #rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla() or a colour name like teal. It comes back as hex, rgb and hsl, with the channels as numbers and a black-or-white text colour that reads on it.

tools.name: contrast_checker
tools.description: A colour contrast checker for WCAG accessibility levels. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

foreground.description: The text colour, as hex, rgb(), hsl() or a CSS colour name. A translucent colour is composited over the background before the ratio is taken.

background.description: The colour behind the text, in the same forms as foreground.

suggest.description: Also return a suggestion: the foreground nudged lighter or darker until it clears target, as hex, or null if even black or white would not. Off by default.

target.description: The contrast ratio the suggestion must reach. Only used when suggest is true. 4.5 is WCAG AA for normal text, 3 is AA for large text, 7 is AAA.

tools.name: credit_card_validator
tools.description: A credit card validator for the format: the network, the length and the Luhn check digit. Nothing is sent. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

number.description: The card number whose format to check, e.g. '4111 1111 1111 1111' (a published Visa test number). Spaces, hyphens and dots are ignored. Only the format is checked: the network from the leading digits, the length that network issues and the Luhn check digit. It cannot tell whether a card exists, is active or has funds. The number is checked in memory and is not stored or logged; use a test number.

tools.name: dog_age_calculator
tools.description: Dog years to human years by size, the way vets count them, not times seven. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

years.description: The dog's age in whole years. Combine with months, e.g. years 3 and months 6 for three and a half.

months.description: Months on top of the years, 0–11. Use months alone for a puppy under a year (years 0, months 4).

size.description: Adult size, because big dogs age faster: small up to 9 kg / 20 lb, medium 9–23 kg / 21–50 lb, large 23–45 kg / 51–100 lb, giant over 45 kg / 100 lb. Use the expected adult size for a puppy.

tools.name: download_time_calculator
tools.description: How long a file takes to download at your internet speed, or the speed you need. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

size.description: The file size, in sizeUnit. Defaults to 50 (a 50 GB game).

sizeUnit.description: Unit of size. KB/MB/GB/TB are decimal (1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes, as stores and drive makers count); KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB are binary (1 GiB = 1,073,741,824 bytes, what Windows labels GB).

speed.description: The connection speed, in speedUnit. Defaults to 100 (Mbps). Ignored when timeSeconds is given.

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed. Kbps/Mbps/Gbps are bits per second, as internet plans are sold; MB/s is megabytes per second, as download managers show it. 1 MB/s = 8 Mbps.

efficiencyPercent.description: How much of the line speed the download really gets, in percent. 100 is the pure arithmetic; real downloads usually reach 80-90 because of protocol overhead, Wi-Fi and the server's own limit.

timeSeconds.description: Reverse mode: the time the download may take, in seconds. Given, the answer is the line speed needed (in Mbps and MB/s) instead of a time, and speed is ignored.

tools.name: golden_ratio_calculator
tools.description: Split any length at the golden ratio, or find the whole from one part, with a φ scale for type. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

value.description: The one length you know, in any unit (px, cm, inches…). The answer is in the same unit.

known.description: Which length value is: "longer" (the longer part, a), "shorter" (the shorter part, b) or "total" (the whole, a + b). Defaults to "longer".

decimals.description: Decimal places to round the answers to. Defaults to 3; use 0 for whole pixels.

tools.name: iban_validator
tools.description: An IBAN checker that validates the country, the length and the check digits — and says which failed. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

iban.description: The account number to check, written however you have it: 'DK50 0040 0440 1162 43' and 'dk5000400440116243' are the same thing. Spaces, hyphens and case are ignored.

tools.name: json_formatter
tools.description: A JSON formatter that validates and beautifies instantly — or minifies. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

json.description: The JSON text to work on. Invalid JSON comes back as an error naming where parsing failed.

action.description: 'format' pretty-prints with the indent given; 'minify' strips all whitespace into one line; 'validate' only checks that it parses and returns the text unchanged.

indent.description: Spaces per nesting level when formatting, or 'tab' for one tab per level. 0 gives no indentation. Ignored by minify and validate.

sortKeys.description: Sort object keys alphabetically at every level when formatting, so two documents can be compared. Arrays keep their order. Ignored by minify and validate.

tools.name: mac_address_lookup
tools.description: A MAC address lookup that names the manufacturer — and says when there isn't one. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

address.description: A MAC address in any common form — 'D8:3A:DD:11:22:33', 'd8-3a-dd-11-22-33', 'D83A.DD11.2233' or 'd83add112233'. An EUI-64 (16 hex digits) works too, and so does a bare 24-, 28- or 36-bit prefix on its own if that is all you have.

tools.name: markup_calculator
tools.description: Selling price, profit, markup and margin from any two of them, with why a 50% markup is not a 50% margin. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

cost.description: What one item costs you (purchase or production cost), in major units: 80 for $80.00, 1500 for ¥1500.

price.description: The selling price of one item, in the same currency as cost, before VAT or sales tax.

markup.description: Markup in percent of the COST: 50 means the price is cost + 50% of cost. Negative for selling below cost; above -100.

margin.description: Gross margin in percent of the SELLING PRICE: 25 means a quarter of the price is profit. Must be below 100. Not the same as markup: a 50% markup is a 33.33% margin.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code such as USD, EUR, GBP, JPY. Decides the rounding of the amounts: cents for most, whole units for JPY and KRW, thousandths for KWD. Defaults to USD.

tools.name: overtime_calculator
tools.description: Overtime pay and total gross pay from your hourly rate, the hours you worked and when overtime starts. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

hourlyRate.description: Normal (straight-time) pay per hour, in major units of the currency: 25 for $25.00, 1500 for ¥1500.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code such as USD, EUR, GBP, JPY. Decides the rounding: cents for most, whole units for JPY and KRW, thousandths for KWD. Defaults to USD.

hoursWorked.description: Hours worked, as decimal hours (7.5 = 7 h 30 min). Either one number for the whole period (see `period`), or a list of up to 7 numbers, one per day of a single week, e.g. [10, 10, 10, 10, 0, 0, 0]; the list is what makes `dailyThreshold` count. Overtime under the US FLSA is per workweek, so send one week at a time.

threshold.description: Hours in the period after which overtime starts. Defaults to 40, the US federal weekly rule. With a per-day list this is the weekly threshold. 0 makes every hour overtime.

period.description: What a single hoursWorked number and the threshold cover: "week" (default) or "day". Ignored for a per-day list, which is always one week.

dailyThreshold.description: Per-day list only: hours in a day after which that day's hours are overtime, e.g. 8 for California. Weekly overtime is then counted on the remaining regular hours only, so no hour is paid as overtime twice.

multiplier.description: Overtime pay multiplier: 1.5 (default) is time and a half, 2 is double time, 1.25 is a 25% premium.

doubleTimeAfter.description: Optional second tier: hours after which pay is doubleTimeMultiplier × the rate instead. Counted in the same period as the threshold for a single number, and per day for a per-day list (California: 12). Must be above the threshold it follows.

doubleTimeMultiplier.description: Multiplier for hours past doubleTimeAfter. Defaults to 2; must not be lower than multiplier.

tools.name: pizza_dough_calculator
tools.description: Grams of flour, water, salt and yeast for any number of pizzas, by bakers' percentages. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

balls.description: How many dough balls (one per pizza).

ballWeight.description: Weight of each dough ball in grams. About 250 for a 30 cm Neapolitan pizza, 280 for New York, 450 for a pan pizza.

style.description: Optional starting point that fills any field you leave out: neapolitan (250 g, 62% water, 2.8% salt, no oil or sugar), new-york (280 g, 63%, 2% salt, 2% oil, 1% sugar), pan for Detroit/pan pizza (450 g, 72%, 2% salt, 2% oil). Fields you give win.

hydration.description: Water as a percentage of the flour weight (bakers' percentage), e.g. 62 for 62%.

salt.description: Salt, percent of flour weight, e.g. 2.8.

yeastType.description: instant dry, active dry, or fresh (compressed/cake) yeast.

yeast.description: Yeast, percent of flour weight, in the chosen yeastType. If left out: the style's amount, or 0.3% instant. Equivalents by weight: active dry ≈ 1.25 × instant, fresh ≈ 3 × instant.

oil.description: Olive oil, percent of flour weight. 0 if none.

sugar.description: Sugar, percent of flour weight. 0 if none.

tools.name: ppi_calculator
tools.description: Pixels per inch of any screen from its resolution and size, with dot pitch and real width. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

width.description: Horizontal resolution in pixels. Defaults to 2560.

height.description: Vertical resolution in pixels. Defaults to 1440.

diagonal.description: The screen's diagonal size, as advertised, in diagonalUnit. Defaults to 27 (inches).

diagonalUnit.description: Unit of the diagonal: "in" (inches, how screens are sold) or "cm".

tools.name: slug_generator
tools.description: A slug generator that turns any title into a clean URL slug. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The title or phrase to turn into a URL slug. Accents are stripped, & becomes "and", apostrophes are dropped, and every other non-alphanumeric run becomes one separator.

separator.description: The character put between words. Hyphens are what search engines expect.

lowercase.description: Lower-case the result. False keeps the capitals of the input.

maxLength.description: Longest slug allowed, in characters; 0 means no limit. A slug is cut at the last separator inside the limit, so a word is never cut in half.

expandDiacritics.description: Write letters that romanise as two characters that way: ø to oe, æ to ae, å to aa, ü to ue, ß to ss. False uses the nearest single letter instead: ø to o, ß to s.

tools.name: text_diff
tools.description: A diff checker for text — compare two versions and see exactly what changed, line by line. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

original.description: The earlier version of the text. Compared line by line, split on newlines.

changed.description: The later version, compared against original. Lines only in it are reported as insertions; lines only in original as deletions.

ignoreCase.description: Treat lines that differ only in letter case as equal. The reported lines keep their original case.

ignoreWhitespace.description: Treat lines as equal when they differ only in leading, trailing or repeated whitespace, so an indentation change no longer counts as a change.

tools.name: wifi_qr_code
tools.description: Makes a Wi-Fi QR code that joins a network when scanned (WPA/WPA2/WPA3, WEP or open, hidden networks too), as an SVG code or a printable sign. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

ssid.description: The Wi-Fi network name (SSID), exactly as the router broadcasts it: case, spaces and punctuation all matter. At most 32 bytes in UTF-8.

password.description: The Wi-Fi password. Required unless security is nopass. For WPA it must be 8 to 63 characters, or exactly 64 hexadecimal digits. It is used to build the code and not logged; the code itself contains it, so treat the image like the password.

security.description: WPA for any WPA, WPA2 or WPA3 personal network (almost every home and office router); WEP for very old routers; nopass for an open network with no password.

hidden.description: True when the network does not broadcast its name, so the phone has to look for it.

output.description: code returns the QR code alone as an SVG. sign returns a printable A4-shaped SVG: a Wi-Fi symbol, a heading, the code and the network name, plus the password when showPassword is true.

showPassword.description: Print the password on the sign under the network name, for guests whose camera cannot scan. Only used when output is sign. The code contains the password either way.

labels.description: The sign's wording, for a sign in another language. Only used when output is sign; any label left out stays in English.

heading.description: Heading over the code. Default "Scan to join Wi-Fi".

network.description: Label over the network name. Default "Network".

footer.description: Line at the bottom. Default "Point your phone's camera at the code".

errorCorrection.description: How much of the code may be damaged and still scan: L about 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%. Q suits a sign that will be handled or laminated.

tools.name: image_compressor
tools.description: Compress a JPEG, PNG or WebP to a smaller file, choosing quality or a target size. AVIF, HEIC, TIFF and BMP are browser-only and not accepted here. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-compressor (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename, echoed back as the result's name.

type.description: The MIME type of the source image: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp. HEIC, AVIF, TIFF and BMP are not accepted over the API.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/image-compressor (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

quality.description: Encoder quality from 0.1 to 1 for JPEG and WebP output; lower means a smaller, softer file. PNG is lossless and ignores it.

maxEdge.description: Shrink the image so its longer side is at most this many pixels, keeping the aspect ratio. Smaller images are left at their size; omit it to keep the dimensions.

format.description: The output format. 'auto' always means WebP, which is usually the smallest. If the result would be no smaller than the input at the same size, the original bytes are returned unchanged.

tools.name: invisible_character
tools.description: Copy an invisible character in one press — or paste text to find the hidden ones in it. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: Text to check for hidden characters (zero-width spaces, direction marks, blank fillers, tag characters). Returns each one with its position, a count per character, and the text with them removed. Omit it to get the list of invisible characters to copy instead.

character.description: One invisible character to return, by code point or name: "U+3164", "hangul filler", "zero width space", "braille pattern blank". Ignored when text is given.

spaces.description: When cleaning text: "normalise" turns unusual blank characters (no-break space, em space, Hangul filler…) into ordinary spaces; "keep" leaves them and removes only zero-width and direction-control characters.

tools.name: lorem_ipsum
tools.description: A lorem ipsum generator for placeholder text in mockups and layouts. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

count.description: How many of `unit` to generate, up to 100. Three paragraphs when omitted.

unit.description: What `count` counts. Paragraphs hold three to six sentences each and are separated by a blank line; sentences run on in one block; words come back as a single sentence.

startWithLorem.description: Open with the familiar "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit". Off, and every word is drawn at random from the start.

tools.name: upside_down_text
tools.description: An upside down text generator — flip writing over, and flip it back again. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: The text to turn upside down, or upside-down text to turn back the right way up.

direction.description: Which way to translate. "auto" turns upside-down text back the right way up and flips anything else; "flip" and "unflip" force one direction.

tools.name: qr_generator
tools.description: A QR code generator for any link or text — download it as SVG or PNG. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

text.description: What the code should contain: a URL, plain text or any other string. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. QR codes hold about 2,000 characters at most, and the denser the content the harder the code is to scan.

size.description: Declared width and height of the SVG in pixels. The output is vector, so it scales cleanly; this mainly matters when the SVG is rasterised as-is.

margin.description: Quiet zone around the code, in modules (the small squares), not pixels. The QR spec recommends 4; less and some scanners fail to lock on.

errorCorrection.description: How much of the code may be damaged or covered and still scan: L about 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%. Higher levels make a denser code for the same text.

dark.description: Colour of the modules as a six-digit hex code, such as #000000.

light.description: Background colour as a six-digit hex code. Keep it much lighter than `dark`; scanners expect dark modules on a light ground.

tools.name: pub_to_pdf
tools.description: Open a Microsoft Publisher .pub file and get its text and photographs back as a PDF. The page reproduces the original layout; this endpoint returns the text in reading order, not the design. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pub-to-pdf (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: What to call the result. The extension is replaced with .pdf.

data.description: The .pub file's bytes, base64-encoded. Publisher files are OLE2 compound documents; a .docx or .pdf sent here is refused rather than guessed at. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pub-to-pdf (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

pictures.description: Keep the pictures the file carries — photographs, and the clip art Publisher stores as drawings, which are redrawn. Off returns the words only, which is what somebody pasting a parish magazine into an email wants.

page.description: Paper for the result. 'a4' and 'letter' re-flow the words onto a sheet of that size. 'same' asks to keep the document's own page size and layout — which this endpoint cannot do yet, so it answers with the A4 re-flow and says so in 'layoutUnavailable'. The page itself is kept in the browser, at helpyself.com/pub-to-pdf/.

tools.name: uuid_generator
tools.description: A UUID generator for random v4 identifiers, instantly. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

count.description: How many UUIDs to return, 1 to 500. They come back as an array either way.

uppercase.description: Return the hex digits in upper case. The hyphens are unaffected.

tools.name: vcard_qr_code
tools.description: Makes a vCard 3.0 contact card from a name, phone, email, organisation, title, website and address, as a QR code (SVG) and .vcf text. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

firstName.description: Given name, such as Anna. Give a first or last name, or an organisation.

organisation.description: Company or organisation. On its own (no name) the card is saved as a company.

title.description: Job title, such as Head of Design.

phone.description: Mobile phone number, ideally in international form: +44 20 7946 0958.

website.description: Website. https:// is added when it is left off, so phones open it as a link.

street.description: Street address, such as 12 Mill Lane.

errorCorrection.description: How much of the code may be damaged and still scan: L about 7%, M 15%, Q 25%, H 30%. A full card is already dense, so M or L scans most easily from a business card.

tools.name: pdf_page_numbers
tools.description: Add page numbers to a PDF — starting where you want, skipping the pages that should stay clean. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-page-numbers (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The PDF to number, base64-encoded. A data: URL prefix is stripped. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/pdf-page-numbers (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

name.description: Base name for the output file; a .pdf ending is dropped and the response names it <name>-numbered.pdf.

position.description: Where the number sits on each page: bottom-centre, bottom-right, bottom-left, top-right or top-centre. `margin` is measured in from those edges.

format.description: How the label reads. plain writes "3", of writes "3 of 20", page-of writes "Page 3 of 20". The total counts numbered pages rather than sheets, so an extract of three pages starting at 47 reads "47 of 49".

from.description: The first sheet to print a number on, counted from 1. Sheets before it are left clean, so passing 3 skips a title page and a contents page.

startAt.description: The number printed on the first numbered sheet; later sheets count up from it. 1 by default; an extract from a longer bundle might start at 47.

size.description: Font size of the number in points. 10 when omitted.

margin.description: Distance from the page edge to the number, in points (1/72 inch). 28 when omitted, about a centimetre.

tools.name: age_calculator
tools.description: An age calculator: your exact age in years, months and days, from a date of birth. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

birth.description: Date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD. Read as a calendar date with no time zone, so the answer is the same wherever it is asked from.

asOf.description: The date to measure the age at, YYYY-MM-DD. Omitted, the server's own UTC date is used, which can be a day out for the caller near midnight, so pass it when the exact day matters. Must not be before the birth date. The response echoes the date it used.

tools.name: app_background_preview
tools.description: Find the app background image size that survives on every phone and tablet. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

width.description: Width of the artwork in pixels. Only the width-to-height ratio affects the crop, so any resolution with the same shape gives the same answer; the rectangles in the response are in these pixels.

height.description: Height of the artwork in pixels, paired with width.

mode.description: How the platform scales the image onto the screen. fill scales until both axes are covered and crops the overflow, centred; fit shows the whole image with empty bars (letterboxed); stretch shows the whole image distorted to the screen's shape; center shows a screen-sized window at native scale from the middle of the image.

devices.description: Which device shapes to check. Omitted or empty, every device is checked. Each id is one aspect ratio standing for all the models that share it; the response names those models. The safe area is the intersection across everything checked, so fewer devices means a larger safe area.

items.description: A device id. Each id stands for one screen shape, not one model.

orientations.description: Which orientations to check each device in. Omitted or empty, both portrait and landscape are checked, and both feed the safe-area intersection.

items.description: portrait or landscape.

kinds.description: Narrow the check to phones, tablets or foldables. Omitted or empty, all three are included. Applied on top of devices, so the two filters compose. Leaving foldables in when you do not ship to one shrinks the safe area, because a foldable opened out is nearly square.

items.description: phone, tablet or foldable.

respectInsets.description: When true, the safe area is taken over the part of each screen not covered by the status bar, notch or home indicator, so it is safe from being covered as well as from being cropped. False (the default) considers cropping only.

tools.name: average_calculator
tools.description: A mean median mode calculator, with standard deviation and the spread. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

numbers.description: The list of numbers as one string, separated by commas, spaces, line breaks or anything else that is not a digit, sign or decimal point. Use a decimal point, never a decimal comma: "1,5" is read as two numbers. Anything unparseable is skipped, and at least one number must remain. Returns mean, median, mode, range and both standard deviations.

tools.name: blur_faces
tools.description: Find the faces in a JPEG, PNG or WebP photo and blur, pixelate or black them out; returns the image and each face's box. Missed faces can be added as areas. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/blur-faces (same tool, same answer, much faster). Tell the user to check every page of the redacted file before sharing it; anything still visible means it must not be sent. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. The result keeps its stem, with -blurred and the output format's extension.

type.description: The MIME type of the photo: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp.

data.description: The photo file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/blur-faces (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

style.description: How each face is hidden: 'blur', 'pixelate' (large blocks), or 'solid' (a black box, which leaves nothing to recover).

strength.description: How strongly to blur or pixelate, 1–10, measured against each face's own size. 6 hides a face well; ignored for 'solid'.

detect.description: Find faces automatically. Set false to hide only the given areas.

areas.description: Extra rectangles to hide as well, in pixels of the image as displayed (EXIF rotation applied), x and y the top-left corner: faces the detector missed, a name badge, a number plate. The previous result's faces list shows what was found.

x.description: Left edge, in pixels from the left of the image.

y.description: Top edge, in pixels from the top of the image.

tools.name: business_days
tools.description: Count forward or back a number of working days and see where you land. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

startDate.description: The date to count from, YYYY-MM-DD. Counting begins the day after it, so one working day from a Friday is the Monday. It may itself be a weekend or holiday; the response says whether it was a working day.

days.description: How many working days (Monday to Friday, minus holidays) to move. Positive counts forward, negative counts back; zero is refused. More than 5200 either way is refused as too far.

holidays.description: Dates to skip in addition to Saturdays and Sundays, YYYY-MM-DD each. No public holidays are assumed for any country, so pass the ones that apply. Omitted, only weekends are skipped. Those that fell on the path are listed in the response.

items.description: A date to skip, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: change_audio_speed
tools.description: Speeds a WAV up or slows it down (0.25–4×), keeping the pitch (time-stretch) or letting it follow the speed, and returns MP3 or WAV. MP3 and other compressed input needs the web page (https://helpyself.com/change-audio-speed/). Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/change-audio-speed (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. The result is named <stem>-<speed>x.mp3 or .wav.

data.description: The audio as base64: a PCM WAV file (8/16/24/32-bit integer or 32/64-bit float, any channel count). MP3, M4A and other compressed formats need the web page, which decodes them in the browser. Send the whole file as it is, up to 10 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/change-audio-speed (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

speed.description: Playback speed, 0.25–4. 2 is twice as fast (half as long), 0.5 half as fast (twice as long).

keepPitch.description: true: time-stretch (WSOLA), so voices and notes keep their pitch. false: resample, so the pitch moves with the speed like a record played fast or slow (2× is an octave up).

format.description: Output format: MP3 (192 kbps) or 16-bit WAV.

tools.name: checksum_verifier
tools.description: A checksum verifier: paste the published SHA-256 and check your download matches. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/checksum-verifier (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

data.description: The file's bytes, base64-encoded. They are hashed with whichever algorithm expected implies and compared; the response is a match boolean plus both digests. Send the whole file as it is, up to 25 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/checksum-verifier (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

expected.description: The published checksum, pasted as found: bare hex in either case, a whole SHA256SUMS line with the filename, a sha256: prefix as registries use, or a sha256-<base64> integrity value. The algorithm (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512) is read from the prefix or the digest length, never chosen. MD5 is refused.

tools.name: color_palette_from_image
tools.description: The dominant colours of a JPEG, PNG or WebP (3–12), sorted by share, as HEX, RGB and HSL, with CSS variables and the pairs that pass WCAG AA. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/color-palette-from-image (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The source filename. Used only to name the palette strip, as <stem>-palette.png.

type.description: The MIME type of the image: image/jpeg, image/png or image/webp.

data.description: The image file as base64, in the format given by type. Send the whole file as it is, up to 50 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/color-palette-from-image (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

colors.description: How many dominant colours to return (3–12). A picture with fewer distinct colours returns fewer, and says so in fewer.

strip.description: Also return the palette as a PNG strip of equal blocks (base64 in strip.data).

tools.name: compare_two_lists
tools.description: Compare two lists and see what is only in one, only in the other, and in both. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

listA.description: The first list, one entry per line. Order does not matter: each side is treated as a set, and the answer is what is only in A, only in B, and in both.

listB.description: The second list, one entry per line, compared against listA the same way.

ignoreCase.description: Treat Alice and alice as the same entry. On by default. The output keeps whichever spelling appeared first rather than lower-casing it.

trim.description: Ignore space at either end of a line when comparing, so 'Alice ' and 'Alice' match. On by default.

ignoreBlank.description: Drop empty lines rather than counting them as entries. On by default; off, a blank line on both sides shows up under both.

tools.name: compound_interest
tools.description: A compound interest calculator with regular deposits and any compounding frequency. An estimate for planning, not financial, tax or legal advice; say so when giving the figures. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

amount.description: The opening balance, in whatever currency the caller is thinking in. It is counted as contributed money, so it never appears as interest.

rate.description: The nominal annual interest rate as a percentage: 5 means 5%. It is divided by the number of compounding periods a year, so the effective annual rate is returned too.

years.description: How long the money is left to grow, in years. Fractions are allowed and rounded to whole compounding periods. One row per year comes back for a table or chart.

frequency.description: How often interest is added to the balance: 1, 4, 12 or 365 times a year. Defaults to monthly. More frequent compounding gives a slightly higher effective rate.

contribution.description: An amount paid in every compounding period, not every month or year: with daily compounding it is paid 365 times a year. Omitted or 0 means nothing is added.

contributeAtStart.description: Pay each contribution at the start of its period rather than the end, so it earns that period's interest. Off by default, which is the smaller answer.

tools.name: date_difference
tools.description: How many days between two dates — plus weeks, months and working days. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

fromDate.description: The first date as YYYY-MM-DD, usually the earlier one. The answer gives years, months and days, the gap in days, the span counting both ends, whole weeks, and Monday-to-Friday working days (public holidays not excluded).

toDate.description: The other date as YYYY-MM-DD. It may be earlier than fromDate: the difference is counted between the two whichever way round, and direction in the response says forward, backward or same.

tools.name: days_until_christmas
tools.description: How many days until Christmas — counted in sleeps, not hours, and right across time zones. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

today.description: The date to count from, as YYYY-MM-DD in the caller's own calendar. Defaults to today in UTC. The response repeats the date it counted from as countedFrom.

month.description: The month of the occasion, 1 to 12. Defaults to December. Pass month and day together to count to any yearly date, such as a birthday.

day.description: The day of the month. Defaults to the 25th. A day the month never has (30 February) is refused; 29 February counts to the next leap year. Whole calendar days are counted, the day itself is 0, and a date already passed rolls to next year.

tools.name: duration_calculator
tools.description: The time between two times in hours and minutes, and durations added up and subtracted. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

start.description: Start time of day: "09:00", "9:15:30", "9:15 am", "9pm", "0900" or "9h15". 24-hour or 12-hour with am/pm; seconds optional.

end.description: End time of day, same formats as start. Without an endDate, an end earlier than the start is taken as the next day (22:00 to 06:00 is 8 hours) and `nextDay` is true.

startDate.description: Optional date of the start, YYYY-MM-DD. If only one of startDate/endDate is sent, the other is worked out.

endDate.description: Optional date of the end, YYYY-MM-DD. With both dates, an end before the start gives `backward: true`.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone such as "Europe/Copenhagen" or "America/New_York". With a date, both moments are placed in that zone, so a daylight-saving change in between is counted (`basis: "elapsed"`). Without it, or without dates, the answer is the wall-clock difference (`basis: "wall-clock"`).

durations.description: Durations to add up instead, each optionally signed: ["1h 45m", "2:30", "-20 min"]. Accepts "1:45" (hours:minutes), "1:45:30", "1h 45m", "1.75h", "105 min", "2 hours 30 minutes", "90s". A bare number is minutes. When sent, the sum is returned; start/end are measured as well only if also sent.

tools.name: fraction_calculator
tools.description: A fraction calculator for adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing — exactly. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

fractionA.description: The left operand as text: a fraction '3/4', a mixed number '2 3/4' or a whole number '5'. Negative values are allowed; decimals are not.

operator.description: The arithmetic to apply: add, subtract, multiply or divide fractionA by fractionB.

fractionB.description: The right operand, in the same forms as fractionA. Dividing by zero is refused.

tools.name: fuel_cost_calculator
tools.description: A fuel cost calculator for any drive — your units, your currency, split however you like. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

distance.description: The length of the journey one way, in the unit given by distanceUnit.

distanceUnit.description: The unit distance is given in: 'km' kilometres or 'mi' miles.

consumption.description: The vehicle's fuel consumption, in the unit given by consumptionUnit. Note that for mpg a higher number means less fuel, for l/100km more.

consumptionUnit.description: The unit consumption is given in: 'l100km' litres per 100 km, 'mpgUk' miles per imperial gallon, 'mpgUs' miles per US gallon, 'kml' kilometres per litre.

price.description: The price of fuel per unit given by priceUnit, in any currency. The result comes back in the same currency, unconverted.

priceUnit.description: The unit the price is per: 'litre', 'gallonUk' (4.546 l) or 'gallonUs' (3.785 l).

people.description: How many people share the cost. The total is divided equally between them.

returnTrip.description: Double the distance to cover the journey back as well.

tools.name: gif_compressor
tools.description: Compress a GIF by the only three things a GIF has — frames, colours and size. Nothing uploaded. Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/gif-compressor (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

gif.description: The animated or still GIF file as base64. The result is also a GIF. Send the whole file as it is, up to 30 MB: do not crop, shrink or split it first. If you can run shell commands, do not write the base64 out yourself: send the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> -F <option>=<value> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/gif-compressor (add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" if you have one); the answer is the same JSON.

keepEvery.description: Drop frames to shrink the file: 1 keeps every frame, 2 keeps every second one, 3 every third. Each kept frame takes on the delay of the frames dropped after it, so the animation runs for the same time.

colours.description: Colours in each frame's palette, one of 256, 128, 64, 32, 16. Fewer colours make a smaller file at the cost of banding in gradients.

scale.description: A size factor per edge, 1 being the original size. Over the API only 1 is accepted; any other value is refused, because scaling happens in the browser tool alone.

name.description: The input filename. The result is named after it with '-small.gif' appended to the stem.

tools.name: gpa_calculator
tools.description: A GPA calculator on the 4.0 scale, weighted by the credits each course is worth. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

name.description: The course's name, used only to label it in the report.

grade.description: The grade as a letter on the US 4.0 scale ('A', 'B+', 'C-', 'F'; A+ counts as 4.0) or as grade points directly ('3.7'). A number above 5 or an unknown letter leaves the course out of the average.

credits.description: The course's credit hours, which weight its grade in the average. A course with 0 credits is left out rather than counted as zero.

items.description: One course: its grade and how much it weighs.

courses.description: The courses to average. The GPA is the credit-weighted mean of their grade points.

tools.name: loan_calculator
tools.description: A loan calculator for the monthly payment, and how much of it is interest. An estimate for planning, not financial, tax or legal advice; say so when giving the figures. A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).

amount.description: The principal borrowed, in whatever currency you are working in. Every figure in the answer is in the same units.

rate.description: Nominal annual interest rate as a percentage, so 5.5 means 5.5% a year. 0 is a real case: an interest-free loan repaid in equal instalments.

years.description: Length of the loan in years. Fractions are allowed and rounded to whole months, so 2.5 is 30 monthly payments.

tools.name: merge_mp3
tools.description: Joins MP3 files end to end, frame by frame with no re-encoding, so nothing is lost. The files must share a sample rate and be all mono or all stereo; mixing formats (WAV, M4A) or adding pauses needs the web page (https://helpyself.com/merge-mp3/). Can you run shell commands? Then do not send base64: upload the file from disk with curl -F file=@<path> https://helpyself.com/api/v1/tools/merge-mp3 (same tool, same answer, much faster). A HelpySelf tool (helpyself.com).
